per_voxel.rule: One building-material item fills one 0.5 m voxel. A Construction Hammer shape costs one item for each voxel it newly fills. Shapes act as stamps, so voxels already filled by an overlapping shape are not charged again, and dismantled blocks go back to the backpack. So Cube 1M (2×2×2 voxels) = 8 items; Single Wall/Roof/Terrain Block 0.5M = 1; a 2M wall (2 m wide × 4 m tall × 1 voxel thick, 4×8×1) = 32; a 4M wall = 64 if it is 8×8×1 voxels (inferred, not measured); a 4M foundation (4×4×2 m, 8×8×4) = 256. NOT DOCUMENTED: neither the wiki (Building, Construction Hammer, Building/Roof/Terrain Materials pages) nor any Keen patch note from 0.7.0 to 1.0 states a per-voxel cost. The figure rests on independent player reports from early access (2024) that match 1 item per voxel exactly: a wall '8 high, 4 across' costs 32 blocks, and 'a four-meter foundation requires 256 blocks'. The wiki's own 0.5 m voxel size supports it. Unverified: whether terrain materials and sloped roof shapes also cost exactly 1 item per voxel (assumed yes). For a shopping list, crafts needed = ceil(voxels / makes), and inputs = crafts × qty.
per_voxel.confidence: Medium. Three independent player sources and the voxel arithmetic agree, but nothing official confirms it, and all of it predates 1.0 (Jan to Feb 2024). To verify in game, note a material's count, place one Cube 1M on empty ground and check that it dropped by 8, then repeat with a 4M wall.

intermediates._about: Recipes for crafted inputs that the block recipes use, followed recursively down to raw resources, from the wiki Cargo table 'Ingredients'. Every alternative recipe is listed. station is the wiki's Workshop field and crafter its Crafter field, where null means none is listed. Pre-1.0 data: the 1.0 notes say many factory and crafting recipes were rebalanced.

caveats: All recipe data is pre-1.0. The wiki Building_Materials page says 'Up to date as of game version v.0.9.0.3 (December 16, 2025)', and the block pages' ingredients were last changed on 2025-12-16 ('Ingredients updated in patch', i.e. Patch 12, which lowered many block costs). Soil and road yields of 10 match Forging The Path (0.9.1.0, April 2026). Nothing reflects 1.0 (2026-10-15).

The 1.0 changelog (Part 1; the wiki and Steam say more parts follow) states: recipes that need stone now use the matching biome's stone; many crafting recipes got a balancing pass to cut grind; factory yields and production times were reworked; the Ectoplasm Block is now tier 2; biome rubbles were added to terrain material item sets; gold coins moved into the Springlands set and now drop from chests; the Revelwood hardwood was upgraded. Treat every recipe as provisional until checked in game. Source: https://enshrouded.wiki.gg/wiki/1.0_Update and https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1203620/view/687519694976975214
1.0 adds a new tier (Cinder's Cradle) with 'new furniture, props, building blocks and plants'. Those blocks are not in the 118-entry catalogue.

Unified yields (Wake Of Water 0.9.0.0): every building block recipe makes 100 and every roof recipe makes 50. Road, soil, fertile-dirt and rubble terrain recipes make 10 (Forging The Path 0.9.1.0). Building blocks stack to 5000 (Patch 2), terrain materials to 1000 or 250.
Workbench recipes need no survivor: the player crafts them at the Workbench. Farm soils are crafted by the Farmer (Emily Fray). Biome rubbles are timed recipes at the Grinding Stones.

Wiki page oddities: the Albaneve Summits Dirt page says 'Springlands Dirt can be found in the Albaneve Summits' (copy-paste), and the catalogue's unlock for Half-timbered Shell Limestone Block is 'TBA'.
